text:
Priya (CS): FYI customer ACME reported widespread 401s + huge p95 latency after 15:42 UTC. Ticket CS-9821. They claim their EU clients were routed to us-west and then auth failed.

Keiko (SRE): Can you paste an example request ID and any logs you have? @Jules @Samir please FYI.

Priya (CS): Here's a sample header and the error they sent:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response: 401 Unauthorized. Request-ID: rq_20260317_15:42:13_az1
Their app logs show routing to host: gw-usw2-03 (us-west pool).

Jules (Eng Platform): Hmm. Our routing policy should prefer same-region. Do we have any recent probe/config changes for health-check thresholds or routing fallback? Logs would help (edge probe vs internal probe).

Keiko (SRE): I pulled probe logs for eu-west nodes around 15:41-15:43. The external /health probe returned 200, but internal auth probe returned 500 intermittently. Snippet:
```
2026-03-17T15:41:57Z eu-probe-11 /internal/health 200
2026-03-17T15:42:04Z eu-probe-11 /auth/verify 500 "token invalid for region"
2026-03-17T15:42:08Z route-controller mark unhealthy eu-west (2 misses)
2026-03-17T15:42:12Z route-controller failover to fallback-pool us-west
```
The auth verify failures look like ephemeral token checks failing when requests are forwarded cross-region.

Samir (Support): Customer also reported a billing spike because the fallback touched the on-demand expensive capacity. They're asking for a timeline, mitigation, and credits.

Priya (CS): Repro steps I gave them to demonstrate the issue locally:
1) Send requests with X-Client-Region: eu-west-1
2) Kill heartbeats on two eu-west probe hosts
3) Observe routing flip to us-west and auth 401s
```
# repro
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health; done
# then sudo systemctl stop redwood-probe on eu nodes
```
They confirmed they could reproduce reliably when probes missed.

Jules (Eng Platform): Possible root cause: probe auth and client auth share a region-bound ephemeral key. When the controller routes to fallback, the auth service validates tokens against region-scoped keys, causing false negatives. Also saw a subset of eu probe agents with stale CA certs (rolled last week) which could explain signal drift.

Keiko (SRE): Immediate mitigations I propose:
- Enable sticky-region routing for impacted customers to force eu-west sticky until fix (:thumbsup:).
- Increase heartbeat miss threshold from 2 -> 5 to reduce flapping while we patch.
- Disable auth-region-binding for probe checks (make health probes use a static service token) as emergency.
I'll push config in 5m and roll to 50% canary.

OpsBot (deploy-bot): Started rollout cfg/heartbeat/threshold=5 to eu-west canary (rollout id: 45789). Status: in-progress.

Priya (CS): Customer accepted sticky-region workaround and asked for rollback instructions once fixed. They've also requested billing credit for the spike; CS filed refund request R-1104.

Keiko (SRE): Follow-up: I'll gather impacted request-ids and affected customers, schedule a postmortem, and open a small CL to decouple probe auth from client tokens. Assigning to @Jules for platform change. Will update ticket CS-9821 when we have timeline.

Jules (Eng Platform): I'll draft the PR for probe auth separation and cert refresh. Plan: patch -> canary -> increase heartbeat threshold revert -> monitor for 24h -> full roll.

Priya (CS): Thanks team. I'll relay the workaround and timeline to ACME and keep the CS ticket open.
